summary_zh: 學會用現在完成進行式描述「最近一直…」的症狀，在診間把狀況、時間長短和擔心的事說清楚。

vocab.definition: to start to have a minor illness, such as a cold or the flu
vocab.example: I always come down with a cold when the weather changes.
vocab.example_zh: 每次天氣一變，我就會感冒。

vocab.definition: tired and slightly unwell, usually because you have been working too hard
vocab.example: After three weeks of late nights, she was feeling completely run-down.
vocab.example_zh: 連續熬夜三週後，她覺得整個人都垮了。

vocab.definition: if a pain or illness flares up, it suddenly starts again or gets worse
vocab.example: My back pain tends to flare up when I sit at my desk for too long.
vocab.example_zh: 我在辦公桌前坐太久，背痛就容易發作。

vocab.definition: medicine you can buy without a doctor's prescription
vocab.example: I've been taking an over-the-counter painkiller, but it only helps for a few hours.
vocab.example_zh: 我一直在吃成藥止痛藥，但只撐得了幾個小時。

vocab.definition: a written order from a doctor for a specific medicine
vocab.example: The doctor gave me a prescription for a stronger cream.
vocab.example_zh: 醫生開了比較強效的藥膏處方給我。

vocab.definition: an extra, usually unpleasant, effect of a medicine
vocab.example: One common side effect of this medicine is feeling sleepy.
vocab.example_zh: 這種藥常見的副作用是想睡覺。

vocab.definition: the act of sending a patient to a specialist for more tests or treatment
vocab.example: If the pain doesn't improve, I'll give you a referral to a specialist.
vocab.example_zh: 如果疼痛沒改善，我會幫你轉診給專科醫師。

vocab.definition: to rest and avoid working too hard
vocab.example: The doctor told me to take it easy for a few days.
vocab.example_zh: 醫生叫我這幾天好好休息、別太操。

reading.title: "I've Been Meaning to Get This Checked"
paragraphs: For most of October, Kevin had been telling himself that the headaches were nothing. He has been working on a product launch since September, and by the end of most days he felt run-down rather than ill. An over-the-counter painkiller usually got him through the afternoon, so seeing a doctor kept slipping down his to-do list. He assumed he was simply tired, not about to come down with anything.

Last Monday, however, the pain flared up during a client call and he could barely focus on the screen. That evening he finally booked an appointment. Like many busy professionals, he had no idea how to describe the problem clearly. "I just said it hurts," he admitted later. "The doctor had to drag every detail out of me."

Doctors say the most useful thing a patient can do is explain how long a symptom has been going on and what has changed. "I've been getting headaches for about three weeks, mostly in the afternoon" tells a doctor far more than "My head hurts." It also helps to mention what you have already tried, such as any medicine you have been taking and whether it caused side effects.

In the end, Kevin's doctor found nothing serious. She gave him a prescription for eye drops, suggested a short break from the screen every hour, and told him to take it easy for a week. She also said that if the headaches continued, she would write him a referral to a specialist. Kevin has been following her advice for five days now, and the afternoon headaches have almost disappeared. He has also learned to push back when his calendar leaves him no bandwidth for lunch.

questions.q: Why did Kevin keep delaying his visit to the doctor?
options: He was afraid the doctor would find something serious.
Painkillers helped enough that the problem didn't feel urgent.
His company didn't allow him to take time off.
He had already seen a doctor in September.
questions.explain_zh: 第一段說成藥止痛藥「usually got him through the afternoon」，所以看醫生一直往後排；並沒有提到害怕或公司不准請假。

questions.q: According to doctors, which description is the most helpful?
options: "My head hurts a lot."
"I think I'm coming down with the flu."
"I've been getting headaches for about three weeks, mostly in the afternoon."
"I just need something stronger for the pain."
questions.explain_zh: 第三段直接拿這句當例子，說它比「My head hurts」提供醫生多得多的資訊：持續多久、什麼時候發作。

questions.q: What can we infer about the cause of Kevin's headaches?
options: They were probably linked to long hours in front of a screen.
They were caused by a side effect of his painkiller.
They were a sign of a serious illness.
They started after a client complained about his work.
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：醫生開眼藥水、要他每小時離開螢幕休息，照做後頭痛幾乎消失，可推知和長時間看螢幕有關。文中說醫生「found nothing serious」，所以不是重病。

grammar.point: Present perfect continuous for ongoing situations
grammar.point_zh: 現在完成進行式：描述「從過去到現在一直在持續」的狀況
grammar.explain_zh: have/has been + V-ing 用來說一件從過去開始、到現在還在進行（或剛停但看得到影響）的事，常配 for／since／lately／recently。看醫生時最常用：I've been coughing for a week.（咳了一週，現在還在咳）。對照組：I've coughed three times this morning. 用現在完成式，強調「次數／結果」；I coughed a lot last week. 用過去式，事情在過去的時間點就結束了。know、like、have（擁有）等狀態動詞通常不用進行式。

examples.en: I've been sleeping badly since the project started.
examples.zh: 從專案開始以來，我一直睡不好。

examples.en: She's been taking this medicine for two weeks, and she hasn't had any side effects.
examples.zh: 她吃這個藥兩週了，沒有任何副作用。

examples.en: Your eyes look red. Have you been staring at a screen all day?
examples.zh: 你眼睛好紅，是不是盯著螢幕一整天？

exercises.q: I ___ (feel) dizzy since I got up this morning.
exercises.explain_zh: since 早上起床到現在都在持續，用 have been + V-ing。

exercises.q: "How long ___ this cough?" the doctor asked.
options: did you have
have you been having
are you having
do you have
exercises.explain_zh: How long 問持續到現在的時間，用現在完成進行式。這裡 have 是「出現症狀」的動作意思，可以用進行式；have you had 也可以，但選項中只有 B 正確。

options: I've been knowing my doctor for ten years.
I've known my doctor for ten years.
I'm knowing my doctor for ten years.
I know my doctor since ten years.
exercises.explain_zh: know 是狀態動詞，不用進行式；持續到現在用現在完成式 have known + for。

exercises.q: My knee ___ (hurt) on and off for a month, so I finally booked an appointment.
exercises.explain_zh: 主詞 My knee 是第三人稱單數，用 has been hurting；for a month 表示持續到現在。

exercises.q: Choose the best answer: "You look exhausted." — "I know. I ___ late every night this week."
options: have been working
worked
work
had worked
exercises.explain_zh: this week 還沒結束，而且「看起來很累」是這陣子持續加班的結果，用現在完成進行式最自然。

exercises.q: Which sentence focuses on HOW MANY, not on the ongoing activity?
options: I've been taking painkillers all week.
I've taken four painkillers today.
I've been feeling run-down lately.
She's been coughing since Monday.
exercises.explain_zh: 有具體次數／數量（four painkillers）時用現在完成式 have taken，強調結果；其他三句都在描述持續的狀態或動作。

review.point_zh: 現在完成式 vs 過去式

exercises.q: I ___ the doctor last Tuesday, and she ___ me some eye drops.
options: have seen / has given
saw / gave
have seen / gave
saw / has given
exercises.explain_zh: last Tuesday 是明確的過去時間點，兩個動作都已結束，都用過去式。看到明確過去時間（yesterday、last…、ago、in 2024）就用過去式。

exercises.q: I ___ (never / need) a referral before, so I'm not sure how it works.
exercises.explain_zh: 到目前為止的人生經驗、沒有特定時間點，用現在完成式；never 放在 have 和 p.p. 之間。

options: I've had the flu two weeks ago.
I had the flu two weeks ago, but I've felt fine since then.
I had the flu two weeks ago, but I felt fine since then.
I've had the flu two weeks ago, but I felt fine since then.
exercises.explain_zh: two weeks ago 用過去式 had；since then 是「從那時到現在」，用現在完成式 have felt。一句裡兩種時態各管各的時間。

listening.title: At the clinic

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Dr. Lin
lines.text: Hi, Mark. Come on in. So, what's been bothering you?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Mark
lines.text: I've been having this pain in my lower back. It comes and goes, but it's been getting worse.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Dr. Lin
lines.text: How long has it been going on?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Mark
lines.text: About a month. It usually flares up in the afternoon, after I've been sitting at my desk for a few hours.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Dr. Lin
lines.text: Have you been taking anything for it?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Mark
lines.text: Just an over-the-counter painkiller. It helps for a bit, but it makes me a little sleepy.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Dr. Lin
lines.text: That's a pretty common side effect. Any numbness in your legs, or pain at night?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Mark
lines.text: No, nothing like that. Honestly, I've been so busy that I haven't had the bandwidth to deal with it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Dr. Lin
lines.text: Well, it sounds like a muscle problem. I'll give you a prescription for something that won't make you drowsy, and I want you to get up and stretch every hour.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Mark
lines.text: Okay. And if it doesn't get better?

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Dr. Lin
lines.text: Then come back in two weeks and I'll write you a referral to a physical therapist. Until then, take it easy.

questions.q: When does Mark's back pain usually get worse?
options: First thing in the morning
In the afternoon, after sitting for hours
At night, when he's trying to sleep
After he goes to the gym
questions.explain_zh: Mark 說「It usually flares up in the afternoon, after I've been sitting at my desk for a few hours.」他也否認晚上會痛。

questions.q: Why does the doctor change his medicine?
options: The painkiller isn't strong enough.
He is allergic to the painkiller.
The painkiller makes him sleepy.
He has been taking too much of it.
questions.explain_zh: Mark 提到吃了會想睡，醫生說那是常見副作用，並開「something that won't make you drowsy」。

questions.q: What can we infer from the doctor's question about numbness and night pain?
options: She is checking for signs of something more serious.
She thinks Mark isn't telling the truth.
She wants to send him to a specialist right away.
She believes the painkiller caused the pain.
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：醫生先排除較嚴重的徵兆，聽到沒有才判斷「sounds like a muscle problem」，並沒有馬上轉診。

dictation: I've been having this pain in my lower back.
Have you been taking anything for it?
Come back in two weeks and I'll write you a referral.

shadowing: I've been feeling run-down for the past couple of weeks.
It usually flares up in the afternoon.
I've been taking an over-the-counter painkiller, but it doesn't really help.
Is there anything I should avoid while I'm on this prescription?

prompts.question: You've had a sore throat and a cough for five days. Describe your symptoms to a doctor.
prompts.question_zh: 你喉嚨痛、咳嗽五天了，向醫生描述你的症狀。
prompts.sample: I've been coughing for about five days, and my throat has been sore since the weekend. It gets worse at night, so I haven't been sleeping well. I've tried an over-the-counter cough syrup, but it hasn't made much difference. I don't have a fever, but I've been feeling pretty run-down.

prompts.question: The doctor has just given you a prescription. Ask two or three questions about it.
prompts.question_zh: 醫生剛開了處方給你，問兩三個關於藥的問題。
prompts.sample: How often should I take it, and should I take it with food? Are there any side effects I should watch out for? I've been drinking a lot of coffee to stay awake at work — is that okay with this medicine?

writing.task: You have to miss tomorrow's team meeting to see a doctor. Write a short message to your manager explaining what has been going on, what you've already tried, and how you'll handle your work.
writing.task_zh: 你明天要請假去看醫生、無法參加團隊會議。寫一則簡短訊息給主管，說明最近的狀況、你試過什麼、工作會怎麼安排。
writing.sample: Hi Jessica, I wanted to let you know that I won't be able to join tomorrow's team meeting. I've been getting bad headaches for the past two weeks, and I've been feeling quite run-down. I've been taking an over-the-counter painkiller, but it only helps for a few hours, so I've booked an appointment with my doctor at 10 a.m. I've already shared my slides with Tom, and he's agreed to present the update for me. If the doctor tells me to take it easy for a day or two, I'll work on lighter tasks from home and keep an eye on Slack. Thanks for understanding, and I'll update you after the appointment. Best, Kevin
checklist_zh: 用 I've been + V-ing 說明持續多久的狀況（並加 for／since）
說清楚已經試過什麼（例如成藥）
交代工作怎麼安排、誰接手
語氣禮貌、結尾說會再回報

translation.zh: 我這兩個禮拜一直睡不好。
translation.en: I've been sleeping badly for the past two weeks.
alt: I haven't been sleeping well for the past two weeks.
I've been having trouble sleeping for two weeks.

translation.en: Does this medicine have any side effects?
alt: Are there any side effects with this medicine?

translation.zh: 如果還是沒好，我會幫你轉診。
translation.en: If it still doesn't get better, I'll give you a referral.
alt: If it doesn't improve, I'll write you a referral.
If it still isn't better, I'll refer you to a specialist.

reading.title: Why We Wait Too Long to See a Doctor
paragraphs: Ask a room full of office workers when they last saw a doctor, and you'll get a lot of sheepish smiles. Many of us have been putting off a check-up for months, sometimes years, not because we don't care about our health but because a clinic visit never feels as urgent as tomorrow's deadline. We tell ourselves we'll go once things calm down. Things rarely calm down.

Doctors call this pattern "symptom normalization." When a problem creeps in gradually, we adjust to it without noticing. A stiff neck becomes part of the morning routine; a nagging cough becomes background noise. By the time someone finally books an appointment, they've often been living with the symptom for so long that they struggle to say when it started or how it has changed.

There's also the fear of being seen as a hypochondriac. Plenty of patients play down their symptoms in the consulting room, worried that they're wasting the doctor's time. Ironically, this makes the doctor's job harder. A vague, apologetic description — "It's probably nothing, but…" — gives a GP far less to work with than a precise account of what has been happening, when, and how often.

So what actually helps? Keep a simple note on your phone for a week before the appointment: when the symptom flares up, what you were doing, and anything you've been taking for it. Bring a short list of questions, and lead with the one you care about most, because appointments tend to run short. And if the doctor's explanation goes over your head, it is perfectly reasonable to ask them to slow down or put it in plain terms.

None of this requires you to become an expert on your own body. It simply means treating a medical appointment the way you'd treat an important meeting: show up prepared, be specific, and don't leave until you know what happens next.

options: Symptoms disappearing on their own over time
Getting so used to a slowly developing symptom that you stop noticing it
Doctors treating every symptom as normal
Comparing your symptoms with other people's
questions.explain_zh: 第二段解釋：問題慢慢出現時「we adjust to it without noticing」，例如脖子僵硬變成早晨日常。

questions.q: Why does the writer say patients who play down their symptoms make things "ironically" harder?
options: They try to save the doctor's time but end up giving less useful information.
They exaggerate their symptoms to get more attention.
They refuse to take the medicine the doctor prescribes.
They see too many different doctors.
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：病人怕浪費醫生時間而輕描淡寫，結果描述太模糊，反而讓醫生更難判斷——本意和結果相反，所以叫 ironically。

questions.q: Why does the writer suggest asking your most important question first?
options: Doctors only answer one question per visit.
Appointments often end sooner than you expect.
It makes you seem more professional.
The other questions can be answered online.
questions.explain_zh: 第四段：「lead with the one you care about most, because appointments tend to run short」——看診常比預期短。

questions.q: What is the writer's overall attitude?
options: Patients should learn medical terms before seeing a doctor.
Most symptoms are not worth a doctor's time.
Preparing like you would for a meeting makes appointments more useful.
Office workers should change jobs to reduce stress.
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：最後一段說不必成為專家，只要像準備重要會議一樣：有準備、講具體、確認下一步。作者也明說「None of this requires you to become an expert」。

listening.title: Not just a cold

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Dr. Patel
lines.text: Right, Emily. The form says you've had a cough for — three weeks? Is that right?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Emily
lines.text: Yeah, roughly. I mean, I thought it was just a cold at first, so I kind of ignored it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Dr. Patel
lines.text: Sure. And has it been getting better, worse, or —

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Emily
lines.text: Worse, honestly. Especially at night. I've been waking up two, three times.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Dr. Patel
lines.text: Okay. Any fever? Shortness of breath when you climb stairs, that sort of thing?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Emily
lines.text: No fever. Stairs — hmm, maybe a little? But I've been so run-down lately, I can't really tell what's what.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Dr. Patel
lines.text: That's fair. Have you been around anyone who's been sick? Kids, coworkers?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Emily
lines.text: Half my office, to be honest. Everyone's been coming down with something since the conference.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Dr. Patel
lines.text: Right. Well, your chest sounds a bit wheezy, so I'd like to rule out a chest infection before we jump to conclusions. I'm going to send you for an X-ray today.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Emily
lines.text: Today? Oh — I was kind of hoping to get back to work this afternoon.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Dr. Patel
lines.text: I get it, but a three-week cough that's keeping you up at night isn't something to brush off. Work can wait a couple of hours.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Emily
lines.text: Yeah, okay. You're right. Where do I go?

questions.q: Why didn't Emily see a doctor sooner?
options: She was too busy at the conference.
She assumed it was just an ordinary cold.
She couldn't get an appointment.
She had a fever and stayed in bed.
questions.explain_zh: Emily 說「I thought it was just a cold at first, so I kind of ignored it.」她也說沒有發燒。

questions.q: Why does the doctor want an X-ray?
options: Emily has a high fever.
Her coworkers all have chest infections.
Her chest sounds wheezy and he wants to rule out an infection.
Emily asked for one to get time off work.
questions.explain_zh: 醫生說「your chest sounds a bit wheezy, so I'd like to rule out a chest infection」——要先排除胸腔感染。

questions.q: What can we infer about Emily's attitude at the end?
options: She is still planning to skip the X-ray.
She is annoyed with the doctor.
She reluctantly accepts that her health comes first today.
She is relieved to have a reason to leave work.
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：她原本想下午回去上班（I was kind of hoping…），醫生說明後她回「You're right. Where do I go?」——不太情願但接受了。

dictation: I've been waking up two, three times.
Everyone's been coming down with something since the conference.
I'd like to rule out a chest infection before we jump to conclusions.

glossary.definition: slightly embarrassed because you know you have done something silly or wrong

glossary.zh: 疑病症者、老是擔心自己生病的人
glossary.definition: someone who worries too much about their health and thinks they are ill when they are not
to make something seem less important or serious than it really is
to be too difficult for you to understand
to decide that something is not possible or not the cause
to refuse to take something seriously
